subject: biology
title: Enzymes at Work
welcome_lead: Meet the chemical scissors that cut up your food into pieces your body can use.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on enzymes in digestion at a simple level.
final_note: You can now explain how enzymes break food into useful nutrients.

concepts.def: Liquid in the mouth with enzymes.
Tiny finger-like parts in small intestine.

walkthroughs.body_html: Enzymes are like tiny chemical scissors. They cut large food molecules into small ones the body can absorb. Saliva, stomach and intestines all add enzymes.
The small intestine wall is covered in tiny villi. These give a huge surface area so digested food passes quickly into the blood.
Stomach acid kills germs and helps enzymes work. The stomach has a thick mucus lining so the acid does not damage its own walls.

numericals.q: If an enzyme breaks 50 molecules per second, how many in 4 seconds?
